title: Vienna Rising Again
premise: Bram Fairweather, a Vienna-based financial-crimes investigator, receives a calendar invitation from her handler—sent hours after his body was pulled from the Danube. The meeting draws her into a laundering operation that launders not money but identities, including her own buried past. Hunted by both the network and her own agency, she allies with a defector courier and a street kid who knows the checkpoints better than the police do. At the border checkpoint at shift change, Bram trades her last secret—proof of who she really was—for their lives, and chooses the found family she built over the duty that betrayed her.
about_author: Ansel Nakamura is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across Central Europe before turning to fiction. They live between Vienna and Trieste, writing thrillers about the people who count what others hide.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sleepless in her Vienna flat, Bram receives a meeting request from her handler Marek—timestamped after his drowning. She goes, telling herself it's duty, and finds a burner phone and a key instead. The beat is dread laced with grief, and the first crack in her trust in the agency.

chapters.title: The Clean Room
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the key to a bank archive, she discovers ledgers of 'clean money' that are actually clean identities—lives laundered as thoroughly as cash, one of them bearing her original name. Emotional beat: vertigo, as her buried past surfaces in someone else's paperwork.

chapters.title: The Boy at Schwedenplatz
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, then shifting to sixteen-year-old Dario, a checkpoint-savvy street kid who witnessed Marek's last meeting. He recognizes Bram's face from a photograph in the dead man's coat. Beat: wary connection—two people who trust no one, tentatively choosing each other.

chapters.title: Internal Affairs Calls
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Her agency suspends her, citing Marek's file, which lists her as a person of interest. Her mentor Ilse warns her quietly to run. Beat: betrayal—the institution that gave her a new identity is the one dismantling it, and duty curdles into fear.

chapters.title: The Courier's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram and Nadia (the defector courier) POV. Nadia reveals she carried the ledger for Marek and that the network's broker, Voss, sells new lives to the powerful and erases old ones by force. Beat: reluctant alliance; Nadia's guilt meets Bram's fury and they find common ground.

chapters.title: What the Danube Keeps
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Divers recover Marek's second phone; Nadia retrieves it, nearly caught by Voss's men. She learns Marek was building a case to protect Bram, not burn her. Beat: grief transformed into resolve, and the first proof that love outlasted duty in Marek's final act.

chapters.title: House of Mirrors
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A trap meeting with Voss in a mirrored hotel bar, where he offers her a pristine new identity if she surrenders Nadia and the ledger. Beat: the theme crystallized—Voss sells escape from the self, and Bram must decide whether she still wants to be no one.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. The plan forms: cross at the Nickelsdorf checkpoint during the midnight shift change, when cameras reset. Dario maps every blind spot, and the trio—Bram, Nadia, Dario—becomes a family around a kitchen table of stolen maps. Beat: warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: The Border
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the checkpoint, Ilse intercepts them—not to arrest Bram but to demand the ledger for the agency's own cover-up. Bram trades her final secret: her true identity and the proof of the agency's complicity, broadcast to a journalist's dead-drop in exchange for passage. Beat: climax—love against duty, paid in full.

chapters.title: Vienna Rising Again
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue in spring. The scandal breaks; Voss is arrested, Ilse testifies. Bram keeps neither her old name nor her new one—she takes a third, chosen, with Nadia and Dario at a Danube-side café. Beat: resolution—identity as something built with others, not issued by anyone.
